guideline: Survey with Likert scale items for ITU (3 items), PESL (2 items), and PFA, plus open-ended questions.
Participants answered Likert-scale items for three constructs: intention to use (ITU), perceived empathy skill learning (PESL), and perceived feedback accuracy (PFA).

After the treatment, we measured the intention to use (ITU) by asking three items. We also asked the participants to judge their perceived empathy skill learning (PESL) by asking two items that covered cognitive and emotional empathy skills. Finally, we surveyed the perceived feedback accuracy (PFA) to control the accuracy of our model. All constructs were measured with a 1-to-7 point Likert scale (1: totally disagree to 7: totally agree, with 4 being a neutral statement).

changes_made.explanation: Removed all human evaluation metadata since this is not an NLG paper. The human evaluation was about system usability and perceived accuracy of classification, not about evaluating generated text quality.

overall_notes: This paper was incorrectly classified as addressing NLG tasks. It is actually a text classification paper focused on empathy detection in student writing. The main contributions are: (1) empathy annotation scheme, (2) empathy-annotated corpus, (3) classification models for empathy detection, and (4) evaluation of a writing support system that provides empathy feedback. The 'feedback' mentioned refers to analysis/scoring of empathy levels in existing text, not generating new empathetic text.
